The copy names real Pearland subdivisions (Shadow Creek Ranch, Silverlake, Silvercreek, Southern Trails, City Park, Green Tee Terrace) with accurate builder and acreage details, correctly ties the lake-and-canal layout to humidity problems, and cites local specifics a resident would confirm — Medical Center commuters on night shifts, year-round AC, and the February–April oak pollen film — none of which could be transplanted to a neighbouring suburb without becoming wrong.

The copy differentiates real villages by actual housing stock and era — 1970s Grogan's Mill with lower ceilings and wide grout versus newer Creekside Park and College Park open plans and two-story entries, with Town Center as the condo/apartment pocket — and ties the work to The Woodlands' defining pine-and-oak canopy, trail-borne leaf litter and shaded rooms that never dry, none of which could be lifted onto a neighbouring Houston suburb's page without becoming wrong; the regional details (oak pollen Feb–April, winter mold peak, year-round AC) are things a resident would confirm, and only a couple of lines about hard water on shower glass would fit anywhere in the metro.

A Memorial resident would recognise the real split between the dense CityCentre condo/townhome stock and the older ranch streets behind it, plus the Gulf Coast damp, oak pollen and January mold-count details that ring true for Houston — though the climate paragraph is really generic to the whole metro ("Late January brings foggy mornings and the year's highest mold counts" would sit equally well on a Katy or Pearland page), and apart from CityCentre no actual subdivisions, streets or landmarks are named.
